'''Harvey Friedman''' (born 23 September 1948)<ref name=hphil>Handbook of Philosophical Logic, {{ISBN|0-7923-7018-X}}, p. 38</ref> is an American [[mathematical logic]]ian at [[Ohio State University]] in [[Columbus, Ohio]]. He has worked on [[reverse mathematics]], a project intended to derive the axioms of mathematics from the theorems considered to be necessary. In recent years, this has advanced to a study of Boolean relation theory, which attempts to justify [[large cardinal]] [[axiom]]s by demonstrating their necessity for deriving certain propositions considered "concrete".

== Biography ==

Friedman is the brother of mathematician [[Sy Friedman]]. Friedman earned his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1967, at age 19, with a [[dissertation]] on ''Subsystems of Analysis''. His advisor was [[Gerald Sacks]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=12036}}</ref> Friedman received the [[Alan T. Waterman Award]] in 1984. He also assumed the title of Visiting Scientist at [[IBM]].<ref>Barwise et al., ''Harvey Friedman's Research on the Foundations of Mathematics'' p.xiii. ''Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics'', vol. 117, North-Holland Amsterdam</ref> He delivered the [[Tarski Lectures]] in 2007.

In 1967, Friedman was listed in the ''[[Guinness Book of World Records]]'' for being the world's youngest professor when he taught at [[Stanford University]] at age 18 as an [[assistant professor]] of [[philosophy]].<ref name=hphil/><ref>[https://u.osu.edu/friedman.8/foundational-adventures/distinctions/ Dr. Harvey Martin Friedman - Distinctions]</ref><ref>[http://www.osu.edu/facultystaff-web/university_awards/2007/lecturer.php Ohio State University Distinguished Lecturers (2007—2008)]</ref> He has also been a [[professor]] of [[mathematics]] and a professor of music.<ref>[http://u.osu.edu/friedman.8/foundational-adventures/degrees-employment-students-contact/ Harvey Friedman's Degrees and Employment History]</ref> He officially retired in July 2012.  In September 2013, he received an honorary doctorate from [[Ghent University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://beeld.ugent.be/nl/fotoalbum/uitreiking-institutioneel-eredoctoraat-aan-harvey-friedman|title=Eredoctoraat Harvey Friedman|last=Friedman|first=Harvey|date=September 4, 2013|website=UGent|archive-url=|access-date=November 7, 2020}}</ref>

== Career ==

Friedman invented and proved important theorems regarding the finite promise games and greedy clique sequences, and [[Friedman's grand conjecture]] bears his name.   Friedman was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers#1974,_Vancouver|invited speaker]] at the 1974 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], with a talk titled "Some systems of second order arithmetic and their use",<ref>{{cite book |last1=Friedman |first1=Harvey |title=Proc. int. Congr. Math., Vancouver 1974, Vol. 1 |date=1975 |pages=235-242 |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm/proceedings |access-date=8 April 2025}}</ref> which established the field of [[reverse mathematics]] by establishing various equivalences between a number of classical theorems in [[analysis (mathematics)|analysis]] in the setting of a weak background [[axiomatic system]]. According to [[zbMATH Open]], Friedman has published approximately 100 [[Peer-reviewed article|peer-reviewed research articles]] and [[conference papers]] during the course of his academic career to early 2025.<ref>zbMATH Open, Friedman, Harvey M., https://zbmath.org/authors/friedman.harvey-m</ref>

Jordana Cepelewicz (2017) profiled Friedman in ''[[Nautilus (science magazine)|Nautilus]]'', describing him as "about to bring incompleteness and infinity out of quarantine.".<ref>[https://nautil.us/this-man-is-about-to-blow-up-mathematics-236446/ This Man Is About to Blow Up Mathematics], by Jordana Cepelewicz, February 17, 2017.</ref> 

Friedman also made headlines in the Italian newspaper ''[[La Repubblica]]'' for his manuscript ''A Divine Consistency Proof for Mathematics'',<ref>{{Cite book |last=Friedman |first=Harvey M. |url=https://cpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/u.osu.edu/dist/1/1952/files/2014/01/ConMathThe122512-1iea8ps.pdf |title=A divine consistency proof for mathematics |date=2012-12-25}}</ref> which was later published in the book ''Ontology of Divinity''.<ref>{{Citation |last=Friedman |chapter=31 A Divine Consistency Proof for Mathematics |date=2024-04-08 |title=Ontology of Divinity |pages=645–696 |editor-last=Szatkowski |editor-first=Mirosław |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9783111332536-034/html |access-date=2025-01-04 |publisher=De Gruyter |doi=10.1515/9783111332536-034 |isbn=978-3-11-133253-6|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In this paper, Friedman showed that mathematics, as formalized by the usual [[Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory|ZFC axioms]], is consistent, if one makes the strong assumption that there is an [[ultrafilter]] with a certain property on the [[Von Neumann universe|universe of all sets]]. Following the ideas in [[Gödel's ontological proof]], such an ultrafilter is considered in Friedman's paper as a mathematical abstraction of the concept of God's existence.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.repubblica.it/scienze/2013/01/05/news/la_matematica_ci_riprova_ecco_perch_dio_esiste-49934292|title=La matematica ci riprova: "Ecco perché Dio esiste"|last=Odifreddi|first=Piergiorgio|date=January 5, 2013|website=la Repubblica|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=December 21, 2018}}</ref> Similarly to Gödel's proof, the argument is purely mathematical, and the theological interpretation of the mathematical assumption is not essential for Friedman's work.
